newsitem.title: CHINA: China bank sees benefits from yuan competition.
newsitem.headline: China bank sees benefits from yuan competition.

text.p: A top official of the Industrial & Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) on Tuesday said the benefits of allowing foreign banks to conduct yuan business will outweigh the threat of new competition.
"We feel there will be competition, but there are more chances for cooperation," said Ji Xiaohui, president of the ICBC's branch in the Pudong development zone east of Shanghai's city centre.

"With mutual cooperation we can advance the construction of Pudong," he told reporters after a loan signing ceremony. "At the same time, this can help Chinese banks to internationalise their services."
The ICBC and the Shanghai branch of Japan's Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi on Tuesday signed an agreement to provide a one year, 30 million yuan loan to the Shanghai Sharp Electrical Equipment Co Ltd.
The joint yuan loan is the first of its kind since nine foreign banks were given approval to conduct local currency business -- the first group at the end of 1996.

"This is the first time for a joint venture to borrow yuan through cooperation between Chinese banks and foreign banks," said Hideki Ariga, general manager for Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi's Shanghai branch.
"We would like to do more dealing in this way," he told Reuters after the ceremony.

The Japanese joint venture, which produces small home appliances at a factory in Shanghai, will use the loan to help begin production of refrigerators and washing machines in July, according to company officials.
The ICBC will provide 20 million yuan of the loan, and the Japanese bank the remaining 10 million yuan. The loan carries an annual interest rate of 9.2 percent, as set by China's central bank.
